title: The passive voice
description: Passive with essere, venire and andare; the agent with da; the si passivante.
objectives: Form the passive with essere + participle in any tense, with agreement.
Use venire + participle in simple tenses and andare + participle for obligation.
Use the si passivante (si vendono case).

blocks.title: Only transitive verbs
blocks.text: Only verbs that take a direct object can be made passive. The object becomes the subject; the participle agrees with it; the tense is carried by essere: *Il gatto mangia la torta → La torta è mangiata dal gatto*. *La torta è stata mangiata* (passato prossimo), *sarà mangiata* (futuro), *fu mangiata* (passato remoto).

blocks.title: The agent: da
blocks.text: Who does the action is introduced by *da* (with the article where needed): *dal gatto, dalla maestra, da Marco*.

blocks.title: State or action?
blocks.text: *La porta è chiusa* can describe a state (the door is closed) or an action (the door is being closed). Context — or the choice of venire — decides.

blocks.title: venire + participle
blocks.text: *venire* can replace *essere* in **simple** tenses only and makes the action, not the state, clear: *La porta viene chiusa alle otto* (is closed every day at eight). Not in compound tenses: *è stata chiusa*, never *è venuta chiusa*.

blocks.title: andare + participle
blocks.text: In simple tenses *andare* + participle expresses obligation: *Il modulo va compilato in stampatello* (must be filled in). With verbs of losing it is simply passive: *La lettera è andata persa.*

blocks.title: si + third person, agreeing with the subject
blocks.text: *Si vende la casa* (the house is for sale), *Si vendono case*. The noun is the grammatical subject, so the verb is plural with a plural noun. In compound tenses it takes essere and agreement: *Si sono vendute molte case.*

blocks.title: Very common in everyday language
blocks.text: Signs, recipes and general statements use it constantly: *Qui si parla italiano. Si cuociono le patate per venti minuti.*

examples.it: La torta è stata mangiata dal gatto.
examples.en: The cake was eaten by the cat.

examples.it: Il castello fu costruito nel Trecento.
examples.en: The castle was built in the fourteenth century.

examples.it: La posta viene consegnata ogni mattina.
examples.en: The post is delivered every morning.

examples.it: Questo libro va letto con calma.
examples.en: This book must be read slowly.

examples.it: In questo negozio si vendono libri usati.
examples.en: Second-hand books are sold in this shop.

examples.it: La notizia è stata annunciata ieri.

exercises.prompt: Il nonno racconta la storia. → La storia ___ dal nonno.
exercises.explanation: Present passive: essere (or venire) + participle agreeing with la storia.

exercises.prompt: I bambini hanno mangiato le mele. → Le mele ___ dai bambini.
exercises.explanation: Passato prossimo passive: sono state + mangiate (agreement with le mele).

mistakes.message: venire is used only in simple tenses: sono state mangiate.

exercises.explanation: si passivante: the verb agrees with libri (plural).

mistakes.message: With the si passivante the verb agrees with the noun: libri → si vendono.

exercises.prompt: *Il modulo va firmato.* What does it mean?
options: The form is going to be signed.

exercises.prompt: Which verb cannot be made passive?
exercises.explanation: Only transitive verbs have a passive; arrivare is intransitive.

exercises.prompt: Translate: The castle was built in 1300. (passato remoto)

summary: Passive = essere (any tense) + participle agreeing with the subject; agent with da.
venire + participle in simple tenses (action); andare + participle = obligation.
si passivante: si vende la casa / si vendono le case; compound tenses with essere and agreement.

title: Impersonal si
description: si + verb meaning 'one, people, you, we': agreement, reflexive verbs (ci si) and compound tenses.
objectives: Use impersonal si with intransitive verbs (si vive bene).
Make predicate adjectives plural after impersonal si (si è stanchi).
Use ci si with reflexive verbs (ci si alza presto).
Distinguish impersonal si from the si passivante.

blocks.title: si + third person singular
blocks.text: Impersonal si refers to people in general: *In Italia si mangia bene. Qui si sta tranquilli. Come si dice 'cat' in italiano?* English uses 'one', 'you', 'we' or 'people'.

blocks.title: Plural agreement of adjectives
blocks.text: Although the verb is singular, a predicate adjective or noun is plural (masculine by default): *Quando si è stanchi, si dorme bene. Da giovani si è più coraggiosi.*

blocks.title: Reflexive verbs: ci si
blocks.text: To avoid *si si*, reflexive verbs use *ci si*: *La mattina ci si alza presto. Ci si diverte molto.*

blocks.title: Always essere
blocks.text: Impersonal si always takes *essere*. With verbs that normally take essere, the participle is plural: *Si è arrivati tardi.* With verbs that normally take avere, the participle stays singular: *Si è mangiato bene.*

blocks.title: Impersonal or passive?
blocks.text: With a transitive verb and a noun, si is passivante and the verb agrees: *si mangiano le mele*. Without a direct object, si is impersonal and the verb is singular: *si mangia bene*. In practice the two are close in meaning.

blocks.title: noi in Tuscan speech
blocks.text: In Tuscany *si* + singular verb is also used in speech to mean 'we': *noi si va al mare* = *noi andiamo al mare*. This is regional, not standard.

examples.it: In questa città si vive bene.
examples.en: People live well in this city. / Life is good in this city.
How do you say 'cat' in Italian?

examples.it: Quando si è stanchi, si dorme bene.
examples.en: When you're tired, you sleep well.

examples.it: In vacanza ci si alza tardi.
examples.en: On holiday people get up late.
examples.note: ci si with a reflexive verb.

examples.it: Si è arrivati tardi alla festa.
examples.en: We got to the party late.

exercises.prompt: Quando ___ giovani, si ha molta energia.
exercises.explanation: Impersonal si + singular verb; the adjective giovani is plural.
Reflexive verb + impersonal si → ci si.

mistakes.message: Two si are not possible: the first becomes ci (ci si alza).

exercises.prompt: Quando si è ___ (stanco), si dorme bene.
exercises.explanation: Predicate adjectives after impersonal si are plural.

mistakes.message: Although the verb is singular, the adjective is plural: si è stanchi.

exercises.explanation: Impersonal si takes essere; with an essere-verb the participle is plural.
With a direct-object noun the si is passivante and the verb agrees with it.

exercises.prompt: Translate: How do you say 'cat' in Italian?
accept: Come si dice cat in italiano?

summary: Impersonal si + 3rd person singular: si vive bene.
Predicate adjectives plural: si è stanchi.
Compound tenses with essere: si è mangiato (avere-verb) / si è arrivati (essere-verb).
